source: Huys et al. (2012) Bonsai trees in your head (PLoS Comput Biol)
finding: Healthy people prune a mental tree after a large loss, even when that is costly. Pruning did not adapt to its cost across groups.
numbers: N=46 (15/16/15 in the -70/-100/-140 groups). Full look-ahead model predicted 77% of choices (mean prob 0.71). Specific pruning beat general pruning in 14/15, 12/16, 14/15 subjects. Pruning did not differ by group. Adding a Learned Pavlovian term: 91% of choices. Losses weighted about 1.4x equal rewards.
limits: Healthy screened volunteers, one 6-state maze. Authors say the depth interaction is not a necessary consequence of the model.
agent_relevance: Pruning at a bad node is a reflex, not a budget choice. S6 pruning rules must be explicit and cost-checked, since a reflex will cut branches behind a salient bad outcome.

source: Huys et al. (2012) Bonsai trees in your head (PLoS Comput Biol)
finding: Pruning was specific to large losses, not general discounting, and survived a control for loss aversion.
numbers: BIC_int: goal-directed model beat habitual SARSA by 314. Pruning & Learned was the most parsimonious model. From state 6 about 90% moved to state 1 with 2+ moves left; about 40% still did with 1 move left.
quote: decisive evidence for specific Pavlovian pruning
limits: Per-group parameters did not improve fit. Some exact p-values were garbled in my extraction.
agent_relevance: Add a check: after a branch hits a disaster, were its good continuations still evaluated?

source: Huys et al. (2012) Bonsai trees in your head (PLoS Comput Biol)
finding: Original claim: BDI score (range 0-15) correlated positively with specific pruning, not general pruning.
numbers: 46 volunteers. Reward sensitivity vs BDI did not survive multiple-comparison correction. No link to NEO neuroticism.
limits: Correlational, restricted range, serotonin story speculative. Later NOT replicated (Lally 2017, Faulkner 2022).
agent_relevance: Do not build agent rules on a mood-linked pruning story.

source: Keramati et al. (2016) Adaptive integration of habits into depth-limited planning (PNAS)
finding: Time pressure moves people to shallower planning that hands off to cached habit values at the depth limit (plan-until-habit).
numbers: N=30, 15 per group. High-resource 2000 ms vs low-resource 700 ms limit. Planning effect stronger in high-resource (rewarded P=0.011, unrewarded P=0.027). Plan-until-habit stronger in low-resource after reward (P=0.034).
quote: speed-accuracy tradeoff controls the depth of planning
limits: Three-step task allows only depths 0-2. Small groups. Authors say one null may reflect fewer samples.
agent_relevance: S6: depth set by budget, with a cheap cached estimate at the cutoff instead of zero.

source: Keramati et al. (2016) Adaptive integration of habits into depth-limited planning (PNAS)
finding: Best model in both groups mixed pure planning with plan-until-habit. Pure habit was not in the best model.
numbers: Stage-2 habit weight 0.37 +/- 0.18 (high-resource) vs 0.59 +/- 0.23 (low-resource). Stage-1 plan-until-habit weight lower in high-resource (permutation P<0.01). Fitted alpha_plan 0.8, alpha_habit 0.55, beta1 8.2, beta2 4.2.
limits: Correlation between stage-1 and stage-2 weights not given in text. Habit values come from the same task.
agent_relevance: Budget cuts should shorten depth first, not drop planning.

source: Keramati et al. (2016) Adaptive integration of habits into depth-limited planning (PNAS)
finding: Cutting a branch with no fallback value is wrong: it gives zero first-stage values and predicts indifference.
numbers: Model result; at stage 2 only depth 0 or 1 is possible in the task.
limits: Theory-driven; one task.
agent_relevance: When the agent truncates, it must still assign a rough value to what is cut, or it cannot choose.

source: Huys et al. (2015) Interplay of approximate planning strategies (PNAS)
finding: People also split a long plan into fragments and reuse sub-plans (memoization), besides pruning.
numbers: N=37 analysed of 41. Fragmentation Spearman 0.44 (depth 3 vs 4), significant in 35/37 (94%). Fragment endpoints matched predictions for 90% of end states. Memoization improved log likelihood in every subject (+43 +/- 22) and explained 14% more variance; full model 78% variance.
limits: One maze. Unrestricted fragmentation overfit (delta iBIC 682 worse). No model of how fragments are found.
agent_relevance: Decomposition into sub-goals plus reuse of sub-results is cheaper than deeper search.

source: Huys et al. (2015) Interplay of approximate planning strategies (PNAS)
finding: Pruning reproduced in a timed version: all 37 subjects discounted outcomes beyond large losses more than other outcomes.
numbers: General discount of non-large-loss outcomes indistinguishable from zero in every subject. A full depth-3 tree needs 24 computations vs 10 when fragmented (over 50% saved). Depth-1 fragments had 9.7 ms longer button delays (t(36)=2.17, P=0.037).
limits: 9 s planning limit changed little vs the original per authors. Verbal IQ not related to fragment length (rho=0.08).
agent_relevance: Independent reproduction of pruning under a time limit.

source: Huys et al. (2015) Interplay of approximate planning strategies (PNAS)
finding: Strategies were stable within people and differed between people.
numbers: One shared fragmentation for all 37 subjects was worse than baseline by delta iBIC 116.
limits: Authors predict the decomposition breaks under changed rewards; untested.
agent_relevance: Do not hard-code one decomposition; choose per problem and check it.

source: Faulkner et al. (2022) A comparison of pruning during multi-step planning in depressed and healthy individuals
finding: Failed replication of the pruning-depression link: unmedicated depressed adults did not prune more than healthy controls.
numbers: 30 depressed vs 31 healthy. Specific pruning 0.617 vs 0.630, t(59)=0.32, p=0.75, BF10=0.27. General pruning 0.136 vs 0.123, p=0.27, BF10=0.44. BDI vs specific pruning r=0.068, p=0.75, BF10=0.26.
quote: there was no group difference in pruning behaviours
limits: Small sample. Mean BDI 25.4. One loss size. Pruning and risk seeking entangled. No neurochemistry.
agent_relevance: The mood account of pruning does not hold. Pruning in everyone stays.

source: Faulkner et al. (2022) A comparison of pruning during multi-step planning in depressed and healthy individuals
finding: Faulkner states the BDI-pruning correlation of Huys 2012 was not replicated in later work.
numbers: Statement only, no numbers given in that passage.
limits: Second-hand within an opened paper.
agent_relevance: Count the depression link as failed.

source: Lally et al. (2017) The neural basis of aversive Pavlovian guidance during planning (J Neurosci)
finding: Pruning replicated in a new healthy sample under fMRI. Depression link not replicated; state anxiety related to it instead.
numbers: N=37 for behaviour (41 recruited). Correct 78% when optimal path avoided large loss vs 37% when it went through one (d=2.06). Pruning on about 52% of suboptimal loss trials vs about 11% chance (range 4% to 93%). Split-half reliability r=0.69. State anxiety link t(37)=2.12, p=0.042.
limits: Healthy sample. Cannot time pruning inside a plan.
agent_relevance: Large, stable, person-specific bias. Design against it.

source: Lally et al. (2017) The neural basis of aversive Pavlovian guidance during planning (J Neurosci)
finding: Model comparison again favoured pruning over simple discounting; the loss deficit grew with depth.
numbers: iBIC: pruning+loss 2466 (55.3% variance), pruning 2472, discount 2549, lookahead 3052. Pruning vs discount delta iBIC 77.5. Deficit at depths 3,4,5: 34%, 40%, 49% (F(2,72)=5.58, p=0.009). Pruning rate did not change with depth.
limits: Single task.
agent_relevance: Deeper trees raise the cost of the reflex.

source: Lally et al. (2017) The neural basis of aversive Pavlovian guidance during planning (J Neurosci)
finding: Neural link: subgenual cingulate tracked the pruning index; insula and DLPFC tracked the specific-general pruning gap.
numbers: SGC MNI(-6,29,-2) t(36)=3.87, p_SVC=0.004. Insula-gap r=0.47 (p=0.003). Pruning trials faster than error trials (p=0.004).
limits: No causal or timing claims; serotonin not tested.
agent_relevance: Pruning is fast and affect-linked, not a deliberate choice.

source: Methamphetamine use disorder multi-step planning study (2025), Huys task
finding: Same task: people with methamphetamine use disorder prune more after large losses, with horizon unchanged.
numbers: 40 users vs 49 controls. Aversive pruning 0.33 vs 0.15, F(1,100)=16.46, p<0.001, d=0.81. Large-loss discounting 0.49 vs 0.33, d=0.74. Horizon p=0.199. Points 2034 vs 3145, d=0.77. Reflective thinking (CRT) linked to less pruning (b=-0.036, p<0.001).
limits: Sex imbalance, cross-sectional, comorbid drug use, small anxiety induction. Not a direct replication.
agent_relevance: Depth and pruning are separable: depth can be fine while pruning fails. Slower reflection goes with less pruning.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Tree search with LLM-evaluated pruning beats sampling at similar node counts on Game of 24.
numbers: GPT-4. IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%, best-of-100 CoT 49%, ToT breadth 1 = 45%, breadth 5 = 74%. About 60% of CoT samples failed after the first step.
limits: GPT-4 only, May 2023. Cost per task much higher; authors say search is unneeded for many tasks.
agent_relevance: Direct support for S6: a small beam with pruning gave large gains on a lookahead task.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Ablations: removing the pruning step or backtracking hurts on mini crosswords.
numbers: Word-level success: full ToT 78, no pruning 65.4, no backtracking 54.6, CoT 38.7 (letter level). Without pruning, 4/20 games solved, 3 of them games pruned ToT could not solve.
quote: better heuristics for DFS pruning are critical
limits: LM pruning heuristic is imperfect and cuts valid branches.
agent_relevance: A wrong prune kills a solvable branch. Keep a way to un-prune.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Breadth is the budget knob: more nodes gave higher accuracy, and search beat best-of-k at equal nodes.
numbers: Game of 24: best-of-100 CoT 49% vs ToT b=5 74%; IO+Refine (k=10) 27%; IO best-of-100 33%.
limits: Matched by nodes, not tokens.
agent_relevance: Spend budget on branching with evaluation, not just independent samples.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Chopping Trees: Semantic Similarity Based Dynamic Pruning (SSDP)
finding: Merging semantically duplicate sibling branches cuts search cost with little accuracy loss.
numbers: Aggregate time speedup vs DPTS 2.26x, Best-of-N 5.20x, Beam 5.94x, MCTS 7.68x. Qwen2.5-1.5B nodes explored: MATH500 11.5 vs 53.3, GSM8K 4.8 vs 19.5; generated 31.1 vs 214.4 and 9.4 vs 79.1. Typically within 5% of best baseline accuracy.
limits: Models 1.5B-8B, math only. Some baseline numbers copied from the DPTS paper. Table partly garbled; clean numbers only.
agent_relevance: Pruning by redundancy is safer than pruning by badness. Add as an S6 rule.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Chopping Trees: Semantic Similarity Based Dynamic Pruning (SSDP)
finding: Authors report an average 85-90% smaller search space; dropped nodes release KV cache.
numbers: Claim across GSM8K and MATH500.
quote: reducing the search space by an average of 85-90%
limits: Authors' own claim; GSM8K ablation on a 500-sample subset.
agent_relevance: Redundancy merge is high yield and low risk.

source: Huang et al. (2026) Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
finding: Sibling continuations from one state are mostly duplicates; sibling dispersion predicts redundancy, so node budget can be set before expansion.
numbers: Llama3.1-8B GSM8K (confidence): tokens 8.22k to 5.43k, time 114.75s to 74.58s. Qwen3-32B: tokens down up to 90% on MATH-500, accuracy comparable. GPT-4o with PRM variance: about 40% fewer tokens. StrategyQA beam accuracy 64.33% to 72.00% with tokens 2.02k to 1.64k.
limits: Preprint dated 16 Oct 2026, not peer reviewed. Accuracy comparable, not always equal.
agent_relevance: Budget rule for S6: spend less where branches agree, more where they differ.

source: Huang et al. (2026) Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
finding: Ablation: the budget part gives most savings; the pruning part focuses what remains on high-value paths.
numbers: GSM8K: 2.63k tokens with budget part only vs 2.69k with pruning part only; both together fewest. Also improved DVTS and REBASE.
limits: Same single preprint.
agent_relevance: Two controls are needed: how many to expand, and which to cut.

source: Li et al. (2026) Spend Less, Reason Better: Budget-Aware Value Tree Search
finding: A budget-aware value tree that moves from exploring to exploiting as budget drains beat a baseline given 4x the resources.
numbers: Four multi-hop QA sets, two model families. OSS-20B: Low tier (5 tool calls) average EM 0.338 vs baseline 0.194; baseline High tier (20 calls) 0.334.
quote: BAVT under strict low-budget constraints surpasses baseline performance at 4x the resource allocation
limits: Preprint, March 2026. Compared only to parallel sampling.
agent_relevance: Closest to 'depth and pruning set by budget'. Sharpen selection as remaining budget falls.

source: Li et al. (2026) Spend Less, Reason Better: Budget-Aware Value Tree Search
finding: LLM self-scores are overconfident, so pruning on absolute scores is unreliable; scoring relative progress is used instead.
numbers: Critic predicts residual value deltas; budget exponent shifts to greedy as budget falls.
limits: No ablation numbers read.
agent_relevance: Prune on change in progress, not on a raw self-rating.

source: Fang et al. (2026) SCULPT: constraint-guided pruned MCTS
finding: Symbolic pruning of implausible MCTS branches (units, types, magnitude, depth) saved effort with small accuracy gains.
numbers: Prunes 34.2% of branches on average (std 3.1; 15 rounds, 3 datasets). GPT-4o-mini: GSM8K 93.8%, MATH 57.2%. Gains +1.1% MATH, +2.0% GSM8K, +1.2% GSM-Hard vs a baseline. Adaptive vs fixed weights 75.8% vs 73.3%. 28% lower optimisation overhead.
limits: Math only; needs task-specific constraints. GSM8K near ceiling (97.8 vs 98.0), within noise. Used inside a workflow optimiser.
agent_relevance: Cheap checkable rules beat LLM judgement for pruning where possible.

source: Callaway et al. (2022) Rational use of cognitive resources in human planning (Nat Hum Behav)
finding: Database record only: a resource-rational account of human planning, a rival to fixed pruning rules. Full text was behind a login redirect and not read.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Candidate rival: strategy chosen by cost-benefit rather than reflex.
